questions.q: Per this lesson, does a CDE record replace the standard dictionary entry fields from Lesson 11?
options: No — it starts from the same base fields and adds more on top
Yes — CDE records use a completely different, unrelated field set
No — CDE records actually remove the owner and status fields
Yes — CDE records never include a definition field
questions.explain: A CDE record still has name, definition, type, owner, status, and last reviewed — it adds four more fields on top, justified by the element's elevated risk.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the four additional fields a CDE record needs, per this lesson?
options: Source system of record
The font used to display the column in a report
The column's exact pixel width in a spreadsheet
The number of times the table has been backed up
questions.explain: The four additional fields are source system of record, validation rule reference, lineage summary, and escalation contact.

questions.q: What is an 'escalation contact,' as distinct from the general 'owner' field, per this lesson?
options: Who is notified immediately when this specific element fails a quality check, often needing faster response than routine maintenance
The person who originally created the database
A synonym for the same thing as the owner field
The vendor who sold the database software
questions.explain: A CDE failure often needs a faster response than routine dictionary maintenance, which is why it gets its own distinct escalation contact field.

questions.q: In the worked OrderTotal example, what does the 'source system of record' field specify?
options: The order management system, explicitly, not the data warehouse copy
A random server chosen at the time of documentation
Every system that has ever touched the data
The name of the person who wrote the documentation
questions.explain: The source system of record names the one authoritative origin explicitly — if an element has multiple apparent sources, that itself is a governance finding worth flagging.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the extra CDE documentation fields are deliberately reserved for CDEs only, not applied to every column?
options: Applying this much documentation effort to every column would collapse the program under its own weight, the same problem Lesson 16 warned about
Because non-CDE columns are not allowed to have any documentation at all
Because SQL Server technically prevents documenting more than four columns per table
Because extended properties can only be attached to CDEs
questions.explain: These fields are valuable specifically because they're rare and reserved for data where the risk genuinely justifies the extra effort.
